note: Authoritative local data from L1 chains.db (DeFiLlama + CoinGecko + growthepie/Dune). Raw signals, no scores. null = NO DATA (do not guess). FRESHNESS: price & market caps are live (today); TVL/stablecoin LEVELS are the latest available (carried forward if a chain's today-point isn't in yet); daily-FLOW metrics (DEX volume, fees, active_addresses, tx_count) are the LAST COMPLETE UTC DAY (today is partial and excluded) — full-day figures, use them as-is. SHARES are each chain's % of the WHOLE DeFi market (all ~500 chains; denominators in market.total_*), so tracked chains sum to <100% and deltas are immune to which chains we track. TVL/volume are USD-denominated, so share moves in a big market swing partly reflect token price, not pure flows. Each chain ALSO carries its OWN raw TVL growth — tvl_change_1d/7d/30d_pct (chain's level vs itself N days ago); use THESE for 'is this chain's TVL growing', NOT the share deltas (share = slice of market, a different question). If tvl_suspect_1d is true the 1d move is a likely upstream data glitch (a >25% one-day swing) — discount the 1d figure and lean on the 7d/30d trend instead. Stablecoins mirror this: stable_change_1d/7d/30d_pct are the chain's OWN stablecoin-supply trend (use for 'is stablecoin capital arriving/leaving', and to confirm or debunk 'stables doubled/halved' claims); stable_suspect_1d flags a >30% one-day swing as a likely DeFiLlama adapter flap (a bridged asset dropping in/out of the index) — call it out as a data-quality event, not a capital flow, and lean on 7d/30d. N-days-ago baselines are median-smoothed, so a one-day glitch can't fake a 7d/30d trend.

# Protocol Changes
* Remove gas rewards: executing a `FunctionCall` no longer pays part of the burned gas back to the contract account as a reward. The `burnt_gas_reward` parameter is changed from 30% (3/10) to 0%. See [HSP-027](https://gov.near.org/t/hsp-027-remove-the-near-developer-gas-rebate/42213)
* Added an `ml_dsa_verify` host function so contracts can verify FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65 signatures on-chain. It takes the signature (3309 bytes), an arbitrary-length message, and the raw 1952-byte public key, each passed either from memory or from a register, and returns 1 for a valid signature or 0 for an invalid one; a wrongly-sized signature or public key aborts the call with `MlDsaVerifyInvalidInput`. The message is verified as-is with an empty context string, so callers must not pre-hash it. It costs a fixed base cost of 540 Ggas and a dynamic per-byte cost of 11 Mgas per byte.
* The per-receipt storage proof limit now applies to every action in a receipt, not just `FunctionCall`. The recorded proof is checked after each action, and a receipt that goes over `per_receipt_storage_proof_size_limit` (4 MB) fails at that action with the new `ReceiptStorageProofSizeExceeded` error; the actions after it do not run. Clients that decode `ActionErrorKind` should expect the new variant. ([#16171](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16171))

## Breaking changes

- **StandardValidator inputs change** (#23870, #23252). `validate` with `ValidationInputDev` takes a new `zkPrestate` field, so its selector changes. Pass `bytes32(0)` for a chain without the ZK dispute game. The `ValidationInput` overload passes zero, so it reports `ZKDG-70` on a chain that has the ZK dispute game. The StandardValidator constructor no longer takes `withdrawalDelaySeconds`.

## Other changes

### Withdrawals and dispute games

- The proof maturity delay on `OptimismPortal2`, the dispute game finality delay on `AnchorStateRegistry` and the withdrawal delay on `DelayedWETH` are now per-chain settings. The L1 ProxyAdmin owner can change each delay with a new setter, within these bounds: proof maturity 1 to 7 days, finality 12 hours to 3.5 days, DelayedWETH 12 hours to 7 days. The StandardValidator checks each delay against its bounds (`PORTAL-100`, `ANCHORP-80`, `DWETH-40`) (#23215, #23252)
- `OptimismPortal2` and `AnchorStateRegistry` fail closed when a delay is zero: a withdrawal cannot finalize and a game does not become final. OPCM rejects a zero delay. A correctly initialized chain sees no change (#23902)

v2.10.3 is a security and stability release on top of `v2.10.2`. It's the public release of `v2.10.3-priv`, which most validators and major RPC providers already run.

No hardfork, no database schema change, no resync required. Nodes can be upgraded one at a time, in any order.

## Highlights

- **Execution**: parallel (BlockSTM V2) balance reads are resolved correctly across a self-destruct boundary (#2403). Shared block caches are size-capped and per-tx code hashes memoized, which lowers importer memory under heavy keccak / ecrecover load. Log counting while tracing no longer copies logs (#2460).
- **Txpool**: pending chains stranded behind a head that can't be mined are evicted after `txpool.strandedlifetime`. Filtered addresses also apply to SetCode (type 4) authorizations. The pool signer is no longer swapped when `allow-unprotected-txs` is set (#2464).
- **Storage trie preload**: segmented BFS queue for the preload, plus optional address-cache persistence across restarts. On a mainnet sentry, preload on restart drops from about 1h25m to about 4s.
- **P2P**: static peers stay dialed across jails and full dynamic slots (#2438), and are kept out of the peer dropper.
- **RPC**: the execution slot is re-acquired between batch items, and the RPC execution pool request timeout from config is applied.
- **Heimdall client**: the configured request timeout is now honored (#2411).
- **Go toolchain 1.26.8**.

governance.title: [Constitutional] AIP: Stylus Activation Contract
governance.body:
## Abstract

This Constitutional AIP proposes to resume Stylus contract activations on Arbitrum One following the Security Council’s pause of new activations: [Security Council Emergency Action – 2/10/2026](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/security-council-emergency-action-2-10-2026/31530). This proposal authorizes a new Stylus Activation Contract and delegates to the Arbitrum Foundation the right to authorize the activation of Stylus contracts that have passed a limited security audit performed by an Arbitrum Security Program auditor (explained in further detail below) and that focuses on whether the code threatens the stability (and security) of the Arbitrum network. The ArbitrumDAO can change or revoke this delegation via a constitutional vote at any time.

Importantly, all existing and activated Stylus smart contracts are not impacted by this proposal or the Security Council action. Any user or developer can continue to use these contracts without restriction, and anyone can continue to renew them through the existing keepalive mechanism. Reactivation of an expired contract, or after a Stylus version change, follows the process in Section 4.
